title: Probabilistic Ship Trajectory Forecasting using Transformer Models on AIS Data
abstract: arXiv:2610.13557v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Anticipation of vessel trajectories is an essential task when navigating at sea. This applies to both human navigators and autonomous surface vessels. Trajectory forecasting enables sub-routines such as collision avoidance to assess the situation and react accordingly in time. This paper investigates Transformer and Performer models for trajectory prediction of surface vessels in confined waters. Using widely available position data from the Automatic Identification System (AIS), candidate models are trained and evaluated. Historical information on how other vessels have moved in the local area surrounding each agent is conveyed using positional heat maps. The heat maps are generated using Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) and encoded with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) before entering the Transformer models. The models are trained with quantile loss to efficiently obtain a model-aware prediction interval, as this is crucial for time

translated_title: 基于AIS数据使用Transformer模型的概率船舶轨迹预测
translated_abstract: 预测船舶轨迹是海上航行中的一项重要任务，这既适用于人类航海员，也适用于自主水面船舶。轨迹预测能够使诸如避碰等子程序及时评估局势并做出相应反应。本文研究了用于受限水域中水面船舶轨迹预测的Transformer和Performer模型。利用广泛可得的自动识别系统（AIS）位置数据，对候选模型进行训练与评估。每个智能体周围局部区域内其他船舶的历史运动信息通过位置热图进行传递，热图采用核密度估计（KDE）生成，并在输入Transformer模型之前使用卷积神经网络（CNN）进行编码。模型使用分位数损失进行训练，以高效获得模型感知的预测区间，因为这对时间……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文利用AIS数据、基于核密度估计的热图编码以及分位数损失训练的Transformer和Performer模型，实现了受限水域中船舶轨迹的概率预测，并给出模型感知的预测区间。
en_tdlr: This paper presents probabilistic ship trajectory forecasting in confined waters using Transformer and Performer models trained on AIS data with KDE-based heat map encoding and quantile loss for model-aware prediction intervals.
